proposal.cover_letter:
Dear Client A,

Thank you for the opportunity to present janitorial services for your two-story corporate office. The proposal covers service five visits per week for the reception and administration office, lobby and mail room, conference room, break room, print room, supply and storage workroom, and both restrooms.

The scope below describes the routine cleaning tasks included for these areas. It is based on the information provided, including that no periodic work was identified during the walkthrough.

Please review the pricing summary below for the approved pricing details. We appreciate your consideration and would be pleased to support your facility’s cleaning needs.
scope_of_work: Clean and disinfect restroom fixtures and high-touch surfaces.
Sweep and damp mop restroom floors.
Offices (including reception / administration, lobby and mail room, conference room, print room, and supply / storage workroom)
Clean accessible glass and interior entrance glass.
Vacuum carpeted areas; sweep or dust mop hard-surface floors and damp mop as appropriate for the surface.
Clean and disinfect counters, sinks, and other accessible work surfaces.
Wipe exterior surfaces of accessible appliances.
Empty waste and recycling containers and replace liners as needed.
exclusions: Floor repairs or restoration, including stripping and waxing or carpet extraction.

benchmark.explanation: The new 2,270-sq-ft bid has five visits per week, matching both office comparables, though it is smaller than their 5,000- and 6,000-sq-ft buildings. Its price is $0.3259/sq ft/month, 2.8% above the tag office’s $0.317, but 40.6% below the public works office’s $0.549. Staffing is 0.767 hours per 1,000 sq ft per visit, versus 0.533 for the tag office (+43.8%) and 0.64 for public works (+19.8%). The bid’s $13.00 hourly wage and 15% profit markup are below both comparables’ wages ($15.50) and profit markups (40% and 75%).
suggestions: Review whether the higher staffing hours per 1,000 sq ft are needed for this smaller office.
Check that the lower 15% profit markup is intentional compared with the office bids’ 40% and 75%.
